(2018)', Lab I, Fig. 5B, 90 s reactivation session, 5 mg/kg systemic propranolol, N = 12, Cohen's d = 1.19) for its positive-control experiment showing that post-reactivation systemic propranolol (PROP) disrupts contextual fear memory reconsolidation in rats. Contrary to the Luna triage objection (which overlooked Table 1 and also used a hyphen-broken non-literal quote from Methods 2.9.6), Bustos et al. (2010) is explicitly included in Table 1 (Lab I, Experiment 1, Figs. 1B and 1C; 3 min and 5 min reactivation sessions; 1.5 and 3 mg/kg systemic MDZ; N = 14, 14, 18, and 18; Cohen's d = 2.62, 5.74, 2.50, and 2.47, providing the 5.74 upper bound of published effect sizes cited in Results 3.1, p. 11) as one of the post-reactivation MDZ amnesia studies conceptually replicated across 20 experiments. In addition, Experiments NS12 and NS20 (Methods 2.9.6, Results 3.6, Discussion p. 15-16) explicitly test pre-reactivation D-cycloserine (15 mg/kg IP 30 min before reactivation) combined with post-reactivation MDZ to boost destabilization as reported in Bustos et al. (2010). The single shipped row (input_row_index 2487, Alfei et al., 2015, doi: 10.1101/lm.038513.115) is a different original study, and Bustos et al. (2010) is an independent empirical publication distinct from Bustos et al. (2006) and Bustos et al. (2009).
